change.author: Julius Marminge

contracts.action: getLimitRecoveryCandidates now excludes, from the fresh-arm branch only, subagent threads whose parent has settledOverride = 'settled'
contracts.equivalent_path: The sweep's own thread-level filter (settledOverride IS NOT 'settled', ProjectionStore.ts:3953) and limitRecoveryCommand's settledOverride check (UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts:29) apply the same rule to the thread itself. The new clause applies it to the parent.
contracts.before_after: Before: a limited subagent of a settled parent got a limit-arm command, then a resume message at reset that woke the parent. After: it is not a candidate until something arms it. A thread already armed (first OR branch, ProjectionStore.ts:3958-3967) still resumes. The test covers that case on purpose.
contracts.visible_effect: Subagent threads of settled parents are no longer auto-armed or auto-resumed after a usage limit. The parent stays settled.
contracts.failure_mode: The SQL clause is read-only. A malformed lineage payload gives json_extract NULL, so NOT EXISTS is true and the thread is armed as before. Nothing is lost.

summary: The SQL change is correct and narrowly scoped. The NOT EXISTS sits inside the fresh-arm branch only, so recoveries armed before the parent settled still resume. The test covers the settled-parent and active-parent cases, both the autoResume and snooze settings, and the already-armed resume case. I found nothing to flag. I read the changed ProjectionStore.ts query and UsageLimitRecoveryWorker.ts. In the test I only checked that the helper symbols (driver, providerInstanceId, modelSelection) and ID imports exist, not the whole file.
